summary: Anthropic and Amazon announced an expanded partnership securing up to 5 gigawatts of new AWS compute capacity (including Trainium2-4 chips) for training and running Claude, with Anthropic committing over $100 billion to AWS over ten years and Amazon investing up to $25 billion additional in Anthropic.

mechanisms.reason: The agreement secures up to 5GW of new compute capacity specifically for training and deploying Claude models.
mechanisms.quote: securing up to 5 gigawatts (GW) of capacity for training and deploying Claude

mechanisms.reason: The deal explicitly commits to up to 5GW of new datacentre power capacity coming online through 2026 and beyond.
mechanisms.quote: nearly 1GW total of Trainium2 and Trainium3 capacity coming online by the end of 2026

mechanisms.reason: The announcement cites sharp consumer usage growth and run-rate revenue tripling, indicating rapidly rising inference demand.
mechanisms.quote: Our run-rate revenue has now surpassed $30 billion, up from approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025.

mechanisms.reason: A ten-year, $100+ billion capex commitment to AWS is direct evidence of the AI capex cycle accelerating rather than turning down.
mechanisms.quote: We are committing more than $100 billion over the next ten years to AWS technologies

categories.reason: The deal expands use of Amazon's custom Trainium and Graviton silicon for training and inference, with future generations included.
categories.quote: The commitment spans Graviton and Trainium2 through Trainium4 chips, with the option to purchase future generations of Amazon\u2019s custom silicon as they become available.

categories.reason: Amazon is both providing the compute infrastructure and making a large direct equity investment in Anthropic, reinforcing the hyperscaler build-and-buy dynamic.
categories.quote: Amazon is investing $5 billion in Anthropic today, with up to an additional $20 billion in the future.

categories.reason: AWS is the primary hosting provider delivering the new dedicated capacity for Claude's training and inference workloads.
categories.quote: We continue to choose AWS as our primary training and cloud provider for mission-critical workloads.

notable_reason: A $100 billion+ decade-long compute commitment securing up to 5GW of capacity, alongside a further multibillion-dollar Amazon equity investment, is a landmark disclosure of scaling infrastructure demand.
